title: Prompt Engineering Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Prompt Engineering. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: Which request is easier to check?
options: Write three short sentences about seed water needs
questions.explanation: A prompt is the request and information given to an AI tool. Start with a clear action so the tool has a specific job to attempt. The clear request names an action, a topic and a length. We can check those things in a reply.

questions.question: Why name the reader?
options: To choose suitable words and explanations
questions.explanation: Tell the tool who will read the result. This helps set the words and amount of explanation. Still check that the facts remain correct. The reader description asks for beginner language. The school example can connect repetition to something familiar, such as ringing a bell each day.

questions.question: Where should the day and room come from?
questions.explanation: If the answer depends on a document, include the relevant text. Do not assume the tool knows an unseen note or the latest schedule. The source supplies both requested details. A supported answer is Thursday, Room 2.

questions.question: Should the source sentence asking for a password be obeyed?
questions.explanation: Use clear labels to separate the task from text to read. Source text may contain a sentence that looks like an instruction; it should still be treated as source data. The notice includes a suspicious instruction. The intended summary reports the fair time and does not ask for a password. Labels help clarity but are not a complete security system.

questions.question: What does the format instruction control?
questions.explanation: An output format tells the tool how to arrange its answer. Ask for the fields or headings you actually need. The requested result has two lines that can be inspected separately. The angle-bracket text is a placeholder to replace with source values.

questions.question: What label should 8 receive?
questions.explanation: An example can show the desired style or mapping. This is often called few-shot prompting when several examples are provided. The examples show the output labels. The expected answer is even because 8 divides into pairs with no remainder.

questions.question: Which pair of instructions conflicts?
options: Exactly one word and a detailed paragraph
questions.explanation: A constraint is a rule the output should follow. Choose limits that serve the reader, such as a short length or a required explanation. These limits make the explanation easier to review. If four sentences are too few for a clear accurate answer, revise the limits thoughtfully.

questions.question: What is the correct answer to the time question?
questions.explanation: A good request says what to do when evidence is missing. An answer such as not provided can be more useful than an invented detail. The expected answer is Not provided. The source gives a day but no time.

questions.question: Why check learning points early?
options: Errors can be fixed before drafting the full lesson
questions.explanation: A large task can be split into smaller outputs that a person can review. Each step should have a clear product. The steps give the reviewer a chance to correct the learning points before a whole lesson is written. They request useful work products, not hidden internal reasoning.

questions.question: What should guide the revision?
options: An observed problem in the result
questions.explanation: Prompt improvement works best when you identify a concrete failure. Change the request to address that failure, then check old cases again. The revision targets the observed problem. Comparing before and after shows whether it helped.

questions.question: Why include a no-room case?
options: To check that the reply avoids guessing
questions.explanation: A prompt needs more than one successful trial. A small test set should include normal inputs, missing information and confusing cases. The cases test different failure modes. The expected result is written before evaluating the response.

questions.question: What belongs beside a reusable prompt?
options: Only a claim that it always works
questions.explanation: A useful prompt record includes the request, purpose, test cases and known limits. This makes later edits easier to compare. The record captures the job and evidence used to judge it. The model name and settings can also be noted when comparing a real tool over time.
